original_question: If κ is measurable, is there a forcing extension that preserves the measurability of κ and makes the positive relation \( inom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} 	o  inom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2\) hold? Likewise, can the same be done when κ is only strongly compact?
target_in_paper: Problem 4.3 in §4, "Polarized partition relations at uncountable cardinals": "Let κ be a measurable cardinal. Is there a forcing extension preserving the measurability of κ in which \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} \to \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 holds? How about a strongly compact cardinal?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the right open problem, the right pair of cardinals ((2^κ, κ)), the right positive partition relation, the forcing-extension setting, the requirement to preserve measurability in the measurable case, and the follow-up about replacing measurability by strong compactness.
missing_details: The notation \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} \to \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 should be unpacked using Definition 1.1: for every coloring c:2^\kappa \times \kappa \to 2, there must exist A \subseteq 2^\kappa and B \subseteq \kappa with |A|=2^\kappa and |B|=\kappa such that c is constant on A \times B.
The paper is asking specifically about the strong polarized relation, not just a generic 'positive relation'; that phrase should be made explicit in a stand-alone rewrite.
The measurable case explicitly asks for a forcing extension preserving the measurability of κ; this should be stated verbatim.

The strongly compact clause is posed elliptically in the paper ('How about a strongly compact cardinal?'); a stand-alone rewrite should make clear that this is the analogous question for κ strongly compact.

The nearby context matters: the problem is motivated by the known consistency result from a supercompact cardinal for the same relation, so the rewrite should stay narrowly focused on weakening the large-cardinal hypothesis from supercompactness to measurable or strongly compact, rather than drifting to the neighboring (κ^+, κ)-questions.
refined_question: Let κ be a measurable cardinal. Is there a forcing extension V^P in which κ remains measurable and the strong polarized relation \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} \to \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 holds; that is, for every coloring c:2^\kappa \times \kappa \to 2 there exist A \subseteq 2^\kappa and B \subseteq \kappa with |A|=2^\kappa and |B|=\kappa such that c\upharpoonright(A \times B) is constant? Likewise, if κ is strongly compact, is there an analogous forcing extension in which κ remains strongly compact and the same relation holds?
justification: This is exactly Problem 4.3. The draft matches the paper almost verbatim, and it clearly targets §4 rather than the singular-cardinal results in the introduction or the later problems about (κ^+, κ). The opening of §4 recalls the known positive consistency result for \binom{2^\mu}{\mu} \to \binom{2^\mu}{\mu}^{1,1}_2 from a supercompact cardinal (Theorem 2.3) and explains that the proof uses generalized Mathias forcing, with supercompactness serving to make the iteration indestructible; Problem 4.3 then asks whether one can lower that hypothesis to measurability, and then to strong compactness. Definition 1.1 supplies the exact meaning of the partition notation, so a complete stand-alone question must unpack it. The only delicate point is the paper’s abbreviated second sentence about strong compactness; making it explicitly analogous is the closest faithful stand-alone reformulation.
